parsed.explanation: The national regime supplies the heaviest visitor-facing exposure: entry officers instructed to refuse cases casting doubt on an applicant's sex with possible lifetime fraud findings; X-marker processing halted (foreign governments issued advisories); trans people barred from government-funded single-sex facilities — a tier-1 universal exclusion reaching airports and federal buildings; and documented abuse in immigration custody (beatings, solitary confinement, sexual abuse) with the state as perpetrator. The division adds a birth-certificate-based facility law covering all schools and colleges (no enforcement mechanism, no documented arrests) and narrowing licence markers. Mitigation is real but partial: no criminalisation of presentation, courts that have enjoined several measures, federal hate-crime and employment protection, 33 municipal public-accommodation ordinances, marriage recognition. Official hostility and majority public support for birth-sex documents keep exposure elevated. Net: high risk.
